text:
Linus Karlsson is having the kind of season that gets noticed slowly, then all at once. Daily Hive called him "an underrated beast" this weekend, and The Athletic's Thomas Drance named him the Canucks' top skater, per Vancouver Hockey Daily. A third-round pick of the Sharks in 2018, he's now an alternate captain in Vancouver with 10 points in 19 games.

The underlying numbers are on his side. Evolving-Hockey had him worth 1.6 wins last season, and their adjusted model had his team creating more with him on the ice than nearly 86% of forwards, despite linemates in the bottom 3% by impact. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking shows him getting to the home-plate area in front of the net more than 88% of forwards, and 59% of his exits leave with possession.

His finishing is right on line (four goals on 4.2 expected), so nothing here looks inflated. Our range puts him between 35 and 55 points over a full season. On a team searching for keepers, he looks like one.
headline: Linus Karlsson, quietly the real thing
